goal: An owner's own look is saved in one place: 'Save as new theme' in the theme editor adds a row to commerce.store_theme_installs (the theme library), the editor has no saved-themes list, and one release later commerce.store_themes is gone.
why: Today an own look can be kept in two places (commerce.store_themes beside the theme library): `rg -n 'store_themes' src --glob '!*.test.*' | wc -l` prints 17. After the second migration it prints 0, and one list holds an owner's looks.

commits.title: commerce.store_themes is dropped; its rows become looks in the theme library (one release after the first commit is live)

changes.how: Only after the first commit is live (/api/health reports it or a later commit). A custom migration made BEFORE the schema change (`pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name saved_themes_to_library`, then `node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs`), so it runs first. One statement: `insert into commerce.store_theme_installs (store_id, preset_id, version_id, title, look, live, installed_by) select t.store_id, null, null, left(t.name, 80), l.look || jsonb_build_object('theme', jsonb_build_object('base', t.base, 'savedId', null, 'settings', t.settings)), false, t.created_by from commerce.store_themes t join commerce.store_theme_installs l on l.store_id = t.store_id and l.live where not exists (select 1 from commerce.store_theme_installs i where i.store_id = t.store_id and i.preset_id is null and i.title = left(t.name, 80));` Then two updates that clear the old pointer: `update commerce.stores set theme = jsonb_set(theme, '{savedId}', 'null'::jsonb) where theme ->> 'savedId' is not null;` and the same for the key look -> 'theme' -> 'savedId' in commerce.store_theme_installs. A saved theme of a store with no live install is not converted: count them in production first (`select count(*) from commerce.store_themes t where not exists (select 1 from commerce.store_theme_installs l where l.store_id = t.store_id and l.live)`) and tell the owner the number before the push.

Remove the table storeThemes (line 9819 on) and, in designPresetUses, the column `savedThemeId` (line 1304) and its index design_preset_uses_saved_theme_idx (line 1319). Remove the table's lines from src/lib/store-copy-rules.ts (line 115), src/lib/personal-data.ts (line 499, and its line in src/lib/personal-data.nb.ts), src/server/store-export.ts (line 49), src/server/store-copy-media.ts (line 82) and, if step 3.5 is done, src/lib/table-classes.ts. Run `pnpm db:generate`: the generated file must hold only DROP INDEX, ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN saved_theme_id, and DROP TABLE commerce.store_themes. If SQL functions in the migrations name store_themes (rg -n 'store_themes' supabase/migrations/*_baseline_1_schema.sql | rg -i 'insert|select|from'), for example the store-copy functions clone_store() or duplicate_store(), replace them in a custom migration without that step, placed before the generated drop.

migration.notes: Only in the second commit, one release after the first, applied by CI. A custom file first converts each commerce.store_themes row into a commerce.store_theme_installs row and clears savedId pointers; then the generated file drops design_preset_uses.saved_theme_id (with its index) and commerce.store_themes. No hot table is touched (stores is updated by a small one-off statement; it is not on the hot list). Running code keeps working because the first commit, already live, reads and writes none of these. The drop removes production rows for good: the owner sees the counts, and a dump is taken if any row exists. Record the versions in docs/decisions.md; check the advisors.
